lane: Intensity: zone by new-fault density, then tile only what clears break-even
hypothesis: A presence-only point-process intensity fitted to the mapped catalogue with mapping-effort covariates (Phillips et al. 2009) predicts where faults the USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue missed should sit; zoning that intensity into 1 km blocks by expected new-fault pixels and lattice-tiling only the blocks above break-even places dots that beat a same-budget uniform-random control on the spatially-blocked hide-and-recover holdout.
mechanism: MaxEnt-form logistic fit (Poisson point-process equivalence, Fithian & Hastie 2013) on 60,988 catalogue presences vs 120,000 uniform background cells over 13 covariates: 4 geophysical edge planes (magnetic horizontal-gradient, tilt derivative, gravity horizontal-gradient, detrended-elevation slope), their max, 5 geophysical regime planes, and 3 mapping-effort planes (1 km / 5 km trace density, relief). Expected new-fault pixels per 1 km block = sum of lambda over non-catalogue cells; blocks above break-even (>= 1 px, the 1% lattice-payment floor) are lattice-tiled at the holdout-derived spacing with a 2 px catalogue collar.
named_non_fault_mimic: Mapping-effort bias itself: the catalogue is a biased sample, so any intensity fitted to it inherits the mappers' footprint (roads, access, quadrangle boundaries) rather than geology; magnetic flight-line levelling residuals and radiometric survey-block edges can also mimic fault lineaments.

representation_aware.note: Overlap legs are reported per direction of support asymmetry and are not operative: at 3 px (300 m) two independent dot fields that both trace the same 60,988-point catalogue necessarily share neighbourhoods. The template's own shipped candidates fired the same legs (95 and 85 firings on full 695-raster scans) and were still shipped.
